name: aws2-sqs
title: AWS Simple Queue Service (SQS)
description: Send and receive messages to/from AWS SQS.
label: cloud,messaging

properties.name: queueNameOrArn
properties.description: Queue name or ARN

properties.name: amazonAWSHost
properties.description: The hostname of the Amazon AWS cloud.

properties.name: autoCreateQueue
properties.description: Setting the auto-creation of the queue

properties.name: headerFilterStrategy
properties.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to map headers to/from Camel.

properties.name: overrideEndpoint
properties.description: Set the need for overriding the endpoint. This option needs to be used in combination with the uriEndpointOverride option

properties.name: protocol
properties.description: The underlying protocol used to communicate with SQS

properties.name: queueOwnerAWSAccountId
properties.description: Specify the queue owner aws account id when you need to connect the queue with a different account owner.

properties.name: region
properties.description: The region in which SQS client needs to work. When using this parameter, the configuration will expect the lowercase name of the region (for example, ap-east-1) You'll need to use the name Region.EU_WEST_1.id()

properties.name: uriEndpointOverride
properties.description: Set the overriding uri endpoint. This option needs to be used in combination with overrideEndpoint option

properties.name: attributeNames
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: A list of attribute names to receive when consuming. Multiple names can be separated by comma.

properties.name: concurrentConsumers
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Allows you to use multiple threads to poll the sqs queue to increase throughput

properties.name: concurrentRequestLimit
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The maximum number of concurrent receive request send to AWS in single consumer polling.

properties.name: defaultVisibilityTimeout
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The default visibility timeout (in seconds)

properties.name: deleteAfterRead
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Delete message from SQS after it has been read

properties.name: deleteIfFiltered
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Whether to send the DeleteMessage to the SQS queue if the exchange has property with key Sqs2Constants#SQS_DELETE_FILTERED (CamelAwsSqsDeleteFiltered) set to true.

properties.name: extendMessageVisibility
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If enabled, then a scheduled background task will keep extending the message visibility on SQS. This is needed if it takes a long time to process the message. If set to true defaultVisibilityTimeout must be set. See details at Amazon docs.

properties.name: kmsDataKeyReusePeriodSeconds
properties.displayName: Kms Data Key Reuse Period Seconds
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The length of time, in seconds, for which Amazon SQS can reuse a data key to encrypt or decrypt messages before calling AWS KMS again. An integer representing seconds, between 60 seconds (1 minute) and 86,400 seconds (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

properties.name: kmsMasterKeyId
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The ID of an AWS-managed customer master key (CMK) for Amazon SQS or a custom CMK.

properties.name: maxMessagesPerPoll
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Gets the maximum number of messages as a limit to poll at each polling. Is default unlimited, but use 0 or negative number to disable it as unlimited.

properties.name: messageAttributeNames
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: A list of message attribute names to receive when consuming. Multiple names can be separated by comma.

properties.name: sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

properties.name: serverSideEncryptionEnabled
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Define if Server Side Encryption is enabled or not on the queue

properties.name: sortAttributeName
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The name of the message attribute used for sorting the messages. When specified, the messages polled by the consumer will be sorted by this attribute. This configuration may be of importance when you configure maxMessagesPerPoll parameter exceeding 10. In such cases, the messages will be fetched concurrently so the ordering is not guaranteed.

properties.name: visibilityTimeout
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The duration (in seconds) that the received messages are hidden from subsequent retrieve requests after being retrieved by a ReceiveMessage request to set in the com.amazonaws.services.sqs.model.SetQueueAttributesRequest. This only makes sense if it's different from defaultVisibilityTimeout. It changes the queue visibility timeout attribute permanently.

properties.name: waitTimeSeconds
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Duration in seconds (0 to 20) that the ReceiveMessage action call will wait until a message is in the queue to include in the response.

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: pollStrategy
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

properties.name: batchSeparator
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Set the separator when passing a String to send batch message operation

properties.name: delaySeconds
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Delay sending messages for a number of seconds.

properties.name: messageDeduplicationIdStrategy
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Only for FIFO queues. Strategy for setting the messageDeduplicationId on the message. It can be one of the following options: useExchangeId, useContentBasedDeduplication. For the useContentBasedDeduplication option, no messageDeduplicationId will be set on the message.

properties.name: messageGroupIdStrategy
properties.label: producer
properties.description: Only for FIFO queues. Strategy for setting the messageGroupId on the message. It can be one of the following options: useConstant, useExchangeId, usePropertyValue. For the usePropertyValue option, the value of property CamelAwsMessageGroupId will be used.

properties.name: messageHeaderExceededLimit
properties.label: producer
properties.description: What to do if sending to AWS SQS has more messages than AWS allows (currently only maximum 10 message headers are allowed). WARN will log a WARN about the limit is for each additional header, so the message can be sent to AWS. WARN_ONCE will only log one time a WARN about the limit is hit, and drop additional headers, so the message can be sent to AWS. IGNORE will ignore (no logging) and drop additional headers, so the message can be sent to AWS. FAIL will cause an exception to be thrown and the message is not sent to AWS.

properties.name: operation
properties.label: producer
properties.description: The operation to do in case the user don't want to send only a message

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: amazonSQSClient
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use the AmazonSQS client

properties.name: delayQueue
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: Define if you want to apply delaySeconds option to the queue or on single messages

properties.name: proxyHost
properties.label: proxy
properties.description: To define a proxy host when instantiating the SQS client

properties.name: proxyPort
properties.label: proxy
properties.description: To define a proxy port when instantiating the SQS client

properties.name: proxyProtocol
properties.label: proxy
properties.description: To define a proxy protocol when instantiating the SQS client

properties.name: maximumMessageSize
properties.label: queue
properties.description: The maximumMessageSize (in bytes) an SQS message can contain for this queue.

properties.name: messageRetentionPeriod
properties.label: queue
properties.description: The messageRetentionPeriod (in seconds) a message will be retained by SQS for this queue.

properties.name: policy
properties.label: queue
properties.description: The policy for this queue. It can be loaded by default from classpath, but you can prefix with classpath:, file:, or http: to load the resource from different systems.

properties.name: queueUrl
properties.label: queue
properties.description: To define the queueUrl explicitly. All other parameters, which would influence the queueUrl, are ignored. This parameter is intended to be used to connect to a mock implementation of SQS, for testing purposes.

properties.name: receiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds
properties.label: queue
properties.description: If you do not specify WaitTimeSeconds in the request, the queue attribute ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds is used to determine how long to wait.

properties.name: redrivePolicy
properties.label: queue
properties.description: Specify the policy that send message to DeadLetter queue. See detail at Amazon docs.

properties.name: backoffErrorThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffIdleThreshold
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

properties.name: backoffMultiplier
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

properties.name: delay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the next poll.

properties.name: greedy
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

properties.name: initialDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

properties.name: repeatCount
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

properties.name: runLoggingLevel
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

properties.name: scheduledExecutorService
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

properties.name: scheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

properties.name: schedulerProperties
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

properties.name: startScheduler
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

properties.name: timeUnit
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

properties.name: useFixedDelay
properties.label: consumer,scheduler
properties.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.

properties.name: accessKey
properties.label: security
properties.description: Amazon AWS Access Key

properties.name: profileCredentialsName
properties.label: security
properties.description: If using a profile credentials provider, this parameter will set the profile name

properties.name: secretKey
properties.label: security
properties.description: Amazon AWS Secret Key

properties.name: sessionToken
properties.label: security
properties.description: Amazon AWS Session Token used when the user needs to assume an IAM role

properties.name: trustAllCertificates
properties.label: security
properties.description: If we want to trust all certificates in case of overriding the endpoint

properties.name: useDefaultCredentialsProvider
properties.label: security
properties.description: Set whether the SQS client should expect to load credentials on an AWS infra instance or to expect static credentials to be passed in.

properties.name: useProfileCredentialsProvider
properties.label: security
properties.description: Set whether the SQS client should expect to load credentials through a profile credentials provider.

properties.name: useSessionCredentials
properties.label: security
properties.description: Set whether the SQS client should expect to use Session Credentials. This is useful in a situation in which the user needs to assume an IAM role for doing operations in SQS.
